- "Clears every movie whose seen flag is true from the watchlist" = a button that removes all watched items.

Cleanest design: one new store operation WatchlistStore.clearWatched() plus a button on the watchlist page that calls it, disabled via the disabled attribute when watchedCount() === 0. The watchlist owner is explicitly told about the new store method so the parallel owners agree on the cross-unit contract.

steps.instruction: Add a new public method `clearWatched(): void` to WatchlistStore. It must remove, in a single operation, every watchlist item whose `watched` flag is `true`. After it runs: `items()` contains only the unwatched items, preserving their relative order; `count()` equals the number of remaining items; `watchedCount()` is 0. If no item is watched it must be a harmless no-op (list unchanged). Persist the change through exactly the same mechanism the existing mutations (add/remove/toggleWatched) use, so the cleared list survives a page reload. Do not change any existing behaviour, exported signatures, or existing tests.

Add a 'Clear watched' action to the watchlist page so a single click removes every watched movie.

Template contract: a real `<button type='button' class='clear-watched'>` with human-readable text mentioning 'Clear' and 'watched' (exact wording is your choice, e.g. 'Clear watched movies'). It must be disabled through the button's `disabled` attribute whenever nothing is watched (e.g. bind `[disabled]='watchedCount() === 0'`) and enabled otherwise; when the list is non-empty but nothing is watched the button stays visible but disabled (do not hide it, do not fake disabled with CSS only). Place it where it fits your layout, e.g. near the progress/watched-count indicator.

Clicking it must invoke a new component method `clearWatched(): void` (see interfaceChange). That method must call the store's NEW method `store.clearWatched()` — WatchlistStore gains `clearWatched(): void` in this same round; it removes all watched items and updates the store's `items`, `count` and `watchedCount` signals. Do not re-implement the filtering yourself; delegate to the store method. After clearing, set the component's `announcement` signal to a screen-reader-friendly message stating what happened and how many movies were cleared (wording your choice), consistent with how `remove()` announces its action.

Do not change existing behaviour or existing tests.
